editorial:
You know the classic Christmas Carol story, but Spirited flips it into a big musical comedy where the Ghost of Christmas Present tries to fix a cynical media consultant and ends up getting roasted instead. Ryan Reynolds plays Clint Briggs, a smooth-talking spin doctor who refuses to be scared by ghosts, while Will Ferrell’s Present is a lovable, overworked spirit who realizes his own life needs fixing. The movie mixes Broadway-style songs, slapstick, and holiday heart, so you get a loud, colorful show that feels like a stage musical on your screen.

The best parts are the chemistry between Reynolds and Ferrell, the catchy dance numbers, and the way it pokes fun at modern PR culture. It can feel long and some jokes repeat, but the energy rarely drops. If you want a cozy, funny holiday watch with big laughs and musical moments, this is a great pick.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Clint and Present finally face their own flaws. Clint chooses to change his manipulative ways and help his niece, while Present accepts that he can move on from being a ghost and live a real life. The twist is that Present becomes human and starts a new future with Clint’s help, turning the usual ghost story into a redemption tale for both men. You leave with a warm, hopeful ending about second chances.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves holiday comedies, big musical numbers, and Ryan Reynolds and Will Ferrell team-ups.
